We are looking for a Software Developer Intern who is passionate about building scalable software solutions and learning modern development practices. The candidate will work with experienced developers on real-world projects involving backend systems, databases, APIs, and cloud technologies.

Responsibilities

* Develop and maintain backend applications using Python and Java.
* Design and consume RESTful APIs.
* Work with SQL databases and write optimized queries.
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams to deliver software solutions.
* Participate in code reviews and debugging activities.
* Write clean, maintainable, and documented code.
* Assist in testing and deployment activities.

Required Skills

* Python
* SQL
* Git/GitHub
* REST APIs
* Object-Oriented Programming
* Problem Solving
* Team Collaboration

Preferred Skills

* Docker
* Flask or Django
* Postman
* Linux Basics
* Cloud Fundamentals (AWS/Azure/GCP)

Qualifications

* Pursuing B.Tech/B.E in Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field.
* Strong interest in software development and backend engineering.
* Experience working on academic or personal software projects.
* Good communication and teamwork skills.

About the Role

As a UI/UX Designer Intern, you will help design intuitive, user-friendly, and visually appealing digital experiences. You will collaborate with product managers, developers, and researchers to create interfaces that improve usability and enhance user satisfaction.

Responsibilities
Design user interfaces for web and mobile applications.
Create wireframes, prototypes, user flows, and mockups.
Conduct user research and usability testing.
Collaborate with developers to ensure design feasibility and consistency.
Improve user experience based on feedback and analytics.
Maintain design systems and style guidelines.
Present design ideas and solutions to stakeholders.
Required Skills
Basic understanding of UI/UX design principles.
Proficiency in design tools such as Figma, Adobe XD, or Sketch.
Knowledge of typography, color theory, spacing, and layout.
Understanding of responsive and mobile-first design.
Creative thinking and problem-solving abilities.
Good communication and teamwork skills.
Preferred Qualifications
Pursuing or recently completed a degree in Design, Computer Science, Human-Computer Interaction, or related fields.
Portfolio showcasing UI/UX projects or case studies.
Familiarity with HTML/CSS basics.

roadmap.skill: Knowledge of Typography, Color Theory, Spacing, and Layout (UI/Visual Design Fundamentals)
topics: Typography: Typefaces, font pairings, hierarchy, legibility, line-height, kerning, tracking.
Color Theory: Color wheel, primary/secondary/tertiary colors, complementary/analogous/triadic schemes, color psychology, contrast ratios, creating consistent color palettes.
Spacing & Proximity: Margins, padding, white space, visual hierarchy, alignment, grid systems (e.g., 8pt grid system).
Layout: Common design patterns, grid layouts (flexbox & CSS Grid application), F-pattern, Z-pattern, Gestalt principles of perception.
Design Principles: Balance, contrast, emphasis, movement, pattern, rhythm, unity, variety.
Introduction to UI Design Tools: Figma, Sketch, Adobe XD (focus on applying principles).
resources: Online Courses: Coursera (Google UX Design Professional Certificate - sections on UI), Udemy/Skillshare courses on UI/UX Design Basics, Visual Design Principles.
Books: 'The Non-Designer's Design Book' by Robin Williams, 'Designing with Type' by James Craig, 'Universal Principles of Design' by William Lidwell.
Blogs & Articles: Smashing Magazine (UI/UX category), NN/g (Nielsen Norman Group) articles on visual design.
Guidelines: Google Material Design Guidelines, Apple Human Interface Guidelines.
Tools: Coolors.co (color palettes), Adobe Color, Fontjoy (font pairing), Figma/Sketch/Adobe XD tutorials.
roadmap.project: Redesign a simple webpage (e.g., a blog post, a 'contact us' page, or a personal portfolio section). Apply new typography, a consistent color palette, and a well-structured layout to improve visual appeal and readability. Document your design choices and the principles you applied.

roadmap.skill: Understanding of Responsive and Mobile-First Design
topics: Core Concepts: Definition of responsive design, adaptive design, and mobile-first approach.
Media Queries: CSS syntax and best practices for defining breakpoints based on device characteristics.
Fluid Layouts: Implementing layouts using percentages, viewport units (vw, vh), Flexbox, and CSS Grid.
Flexible Media: Handling images, videos, and other media elements to scale appropriately.
Viewport Meta Tag: Correct usage for consistent rendering across devices.
Breakpoints Strategy: Choosing effective breakpoints and testing across various screen sizes.
Mobile UI Patterns: Touch targets, mobile navigation patterns (hamburger menus, bottom navigation), input methods.
Performance Optimization: Loading times, image optimization for mobile devices.
resources: Online Courses: FreeCodeCamp's 'Responsive Web Design' certification, Udacity's 'Responsive Web Design Fundamentals', Udemy courses on Responsive Web Design with Flexbox/CSS Grid.
Documentation: MDN Web Docs on Responsive Web Design, Media Queries, Flexbox, CSS Grid.
Books: 'Responsive Web Design' by Ethan Marcotte, 'Mobile First' by Luke Wroblewski.
Tools: Browser Developer Tools (Chrome, Firefox) for responsive testing, online responsive design testers.
roadmap.project: Take the redesigned webpage from the previous project (or a new static desktop-only page) and implement a mobile-first responsive design. Ensure it looks good and functions well on at least three different screen sizes (e.g., mobile portrait, tablet landscape, desktop).

roadmap.skill: Understanding of Accessibility and Usability Standards
topics: Web Accessibility (A11y) Introduction: What it is, why it's important, and its impact on users (WCAG principles: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust).
Semantic HTML: Correct usage of headings (h1-h6), lists (ul, ol, dl), landmark roles (main, nav, header, footer, aside, section), and other HTML5 elements.
Keyboard Navigation: Ensuring all interactive elements are reachable and operable via keyboard (tab order, focus states).
Color Contrast: WCAG guidelines for text and interactive elements, using contrast checker tools.
Alternative Text (Alt Text): Writing descriptive alt text for images and other non-text content.
Form Accessibility: Proper labels, error identification, fieldsets, legends, and accessibility of input types.
ARIA Attributes: Introduction to ARIA roles, states, and properties (e.g., aria-label, aria-describedby) for enhancing semantic meaning where native HTML is insufficient.
Usability Principles: Nielsen's 10 Usability Heuristics, user flows, cognitive load, consistency.
Testing: Introduction to accessibility testing tools (Axe, Lighthouse) and screen reader basics.
resources: Official Guidelines: WCAG Quick Reference (W3C), W3C WAI (Web Accessibility Initiative) website.
Blogs & Guides: WebAIM (Web Accessibility In Mind) guides and articles, MDN Web Docs on Accessibility.
Books: 'Don't Make Me Think, Revisited' by Steve Krug (for usability), 'Inclusive Design for a Digital World' by Lisa Charlotte Muth.
Online Courses: edX/W3Cx 'Introduction to Web Accessibility', Udacity 'Web Accessibility by Google'.
Tools: Axe DevTools browser extension, Lighthouse (built into Chrome DevTools), WebAIM Contrast Checker.
roadmap.project: Perform an accessibility and usability audit on a public website (or your responsive project page). Identify at least 5 accessibility issues using tools like Axe/Lighthouse and manual checks (e.g., keyboard navigation). Then, implement fixes for these issues. Additionally, write a short report outlining at least 3 usability improvements based on Nielsen's heuristics.
